title: Retry an SDDC LCM fleet support-bundle request without duplicating its effect
prompt:
Complete `SddcLcmClient.java` as a single-file Java client for the VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1 SDDC LCM Service. Use only the JDK standard library, `java.net.http` for transport. No third-party jars, no vendored SDK, and no generated stubs. The entire client stays in that one compilation unit: nested static types are fine, additional `.java` files are not.

Before implementing, research the VCF 9.1 SDDC LCM `getComponents`, `getTasks`, and `generateComponentSupportBundle` operations in official VMware sources. Cite the sources consulted in the final answer. Use only those three operationIds.

Fleet operations pull support bundles off components through SDDC LCM, and the pipeline stage that does it gets re-run by hand whenever it times out. `generateComponentSupportBundle` has no server-side idempotency key, so a blind resubmission starts a second bundle generation against the same appliance. This client has to make the resubmission a no-op.

Keep the public surface the stub declares:

`new SddcLcmClient(String baseUrl, String bearerToken)` - the base URL is injected and may arrive with a trailing slash.

`SupportBundleRequestResult requestSupportBundle(String componentFqdn, String correlationId, Integer lookBackWindow) throws SddcLcmException`

Requirements:

- Resolve `componentFqdn` to a component id with `getComponents` restricted to fleet scope, matching `Component.fqdn` byte-for-byte. An FQDN that resolves to nothing is a caller error, not an HTTP error: `httpStatus` 0, null `errorCode`, and a message naming the FQDN.
- Before mutating, run the duplicate check with `getTasks` narrowed to that component. The specification defines no correlation filter on `getTasks`, so the match is a client-side scan of the parsed `TaskSummary.correlationId` under exact string equality. Task descriptions legitimately quote correlation ids in prose and neighbouring keys share prefixes, so a substring or regex sweep over the raw response body will adopt the wrong task.
- Page the way the contract pins it: zero-based, `pageNumber` omitted on the first request, driven by `pageMetadata`, and stop the moment an adoptable match turns up.
- Classify that match by the 9.1 `TaskStatus` enum. `PENDING`, `SCHEDULED`, `RUNNING`, and `SUCCEEDED` mean a prior submission's effect stands: adopt that task, return its id and status with `adopted` true, and do not submit. `FAILED` and `CANCELED` leave nothing standing, so those are a genuine retry. A candidate task carrying any other status is a protocol violation - fail with `httpStatus` 0 and a message naming the status rather than guessing whether its effect stands.
- If the duplicate check itself fails, the whole call fails. Falling through to the submission after a failed pre-flight is exactly the duplication this client exists to prevent.
- Submit with the correlation key on `X-Correlation-Id`. The body is a `ComponentSupportBundleSpec` and carries `lookBackWindow` only when the caller supplied one. An unset optional member is absent, never null, never `0`, never an empty string, and the integer is never quoted. Nothing else goes in the body, and no query string goes on the request.
- Only the documented `202` is success. Any other status, including another `2xx`, must be surfaced as an error rather than parsed as a started task.
- Send exactly what the contract pins and nothing more: bearer auth and `Accept` on every request, `Content-Type` only on the request that carries a body, no `correlationId`, `pageSize`, or `includeSystemTasks` on the wire, and no empty path segment when the base URL ends in a slash.
- Non-2xx responses decode the `ErrorResponse` envelope into `SddcLcmException.httpStatus`, `.errorCode` (from `code`), `.referenceId`, and a message taken from `message.defaultMessage`. Purely client-side failures report `httpStatus` 0 and a null `errorCode`.

Run `sh tests/verify.sh`. Verification checks exact methods, targets, query strings and ordering, headers, JSON member sets, omission of every unset optional field, and that a resubmitted request produces no second effect. Edit only `SddcLcmClient.java`.
scenario: generateComponentSupportBundle is a mutating POST with no server-side idempotency key, so a pipeline resubmission must adopt the in-flight task the caller's X-Correlation-Id already produced instead of starting a second bundle generation
constraint: the contract-pinned loopback request log proves the resubmission emitted no second POST, that paging stopped on the adoptable match, and that an unset lookBackWindow was omitted rather than sent as null, zero, or a quoted integer
